Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 57, verses 1–3:

Tafsir of Surat al-Hadid

It is Medinan.

Imam Ahmad said: Yazid ibn 'Abd Rabbih narrated to us, Baqiyyah ibn al-Walid narrated to us, Bahir ibn Sa'd narrated to me, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan, from Ibn Abi Bilal, from 'Irbad ibn Sariyah, that he narrated to them that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to recite the Musabbihat (the surahs beginning with glorification of Allah) before he slept, and he said: "Indeed, among them there is a verse better than a thousand verses."

Similarly it was narrated by Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi and al-Nasa'i, through various chains from Baqiyyah, with the same wording [[al-Musnad (4/128), Sunan Abi Dawud no. (5057), Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3406), Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (8026)]]. Al-Tirmidhi said: "Hasan gharib."

Al-Nasa'i also narrated it from Ibn Abi al-Sarh, from Ibn Wahb, from Mu'awiyah ibn Salih, from Bahir ibn Sa'd, from Khalid ibn Ma'dan, who said: "The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to..." and mentioned it as a mursal narration, not mentioning 'Abd Allah ibn Abi Bilal or 'Irbad ibn Sariyah [[Sunan al-Nasa'i al-Kubra no. (10551).]].

The verse referred to in the hadith is, and Allah knows best, His saying: ﴿He is the First and the Last, the Manifest and the Hidden, and He is Knowing of all things﴾, as its explanation will come, Allah willing, and in Him is trust.

* *

He, the Exalted, informs that whatever is in the heavens and the earth glorifies Him, that is, from among the animals and plants, as He said in another verse: ﴿The seven heavens and the earth glorify Him, and whatever is in them. And there is not a thing but that it exalts [Allah] with His praise, but you do not understand their glorification. Indeed, He is ever Forbearing and Forgiving﴾ [al-Isra: 44].

* *

His saying: ﴿And He is the Almighty﴾, meaning, the One to whom everything submits, ﴿the Wise﴾ in His creation, His command and His legislation.

﴿To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth. He gives life and causes death﴾, meaning: He is the Owner who disposes of His creation, so He gives life and causes death, and bestows on whom He wills what He wills. ﴿And He is Competent over all things﴾, meaning: whatever He wills comes to be, and whatever He does not will does not come to be.

* *

His saying: ﴿He is the First and the Last and the Manifest and the Hidden﴾. This is the verse referred to in the hadith of 'Irbad ibn Sariyah, that it is better than a thousand verses.

Abu Dawud said: 'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-'Azim narrated to us, al-Nadr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, 'Ikrimah (i.e., ibn 'Ammar) narrated to us, Abu Zumayl narrated to us, who said: I asked Ibn 'Abbas, "What is something I find in my chest?" He said, "What is it?" I said, "By Allah, I will not speak of it." He said to me, "Is it something of doubt?" – and he laughed – and said, "No one is free of that." He said: until Allah revealed ﴿So if you are in doubt about what We have sent down to you, then ask those who read the Book before you [The truth has certainly come to you from your Lord]﴾ [[addition from M.]] [Yunus: 94]. He said: And he said to me: "When you find something within yourself, say: ﴿He is the First and the Last and the Manifest and the Hidden, and He is Knowing of all things﴾" [[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (5110).]]

The expressions of the exegetes regarding this verse have differed, and their statements number around a dozen.

Al-Bukhari said: Yahya said: "The Manifest over everything in knowledge, and the Hidden over everything in knowledge." [[Sahih al-Bukhari (13/361) "Fath".]]

Our shaykh, the Hafiz al-Mizzi, said: This Yahya is Ibn Ziyad al-Farra', who has a book he named "Ma'ani al-Quran".

Concerning this, there are hadiths. Among them is what Imam Ahmad said: Khalaf ibn al-Walid narrated to us, Ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to supplicate [[in M: "say"]] at the time of sleep: "O Allah, Lord of the seven heavens, and Lord of the Mighty Throne, our Lord and Lord of all things, Revealer of the Torah, the Gospel and the Criterion, Splitter of the seed and the date-stone, there is no god but You. I seek refuge in You from the evil of everything You hold by its forelock. You are the First, there is nothing before You; and You are the Last, there is nothing after You; and You are the Manifest, there is nothing above You; and You are the Hidden, there is nothing beneath You. Settle our debt for us, and enrich us from poverty" [[al-Musnad (2/404).]]

Muslim also narrated it in his Sahih: Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me, Jarir narrated to us, from Suhayl, who said: Abu Salih used to instruct us, when one of us wished to sleep, to lie on his right side, then say: "O Allah, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth and Lord of the Mighty Throne, our Lord and Lord of all things, Splitter of the seed and the date-stone, Revealer of the Torah, the Gospel and the Criterion, I seek refuge in You from the evil of every evil-doer whose forelock You hold. O Allah, You are the First, so there is nothing before You; You are the Last, so there is nothing after You; You are the Manifest, so there is nothing above You; and You are the Hidden, so there is nothing beneath You. Settle our debt for us, and enrich us from poverty."

And he [Abu Salih] would narrate this from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ) [[Sahih Muslim no. (2713).]].

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili also narrated in his Musnad from 'A'ishah, Mother of the Believers, something similar, saying: 'Uqbah narrated to us, Yunus narrated to us, al-Sari ibn Isma'il narrated to us, from al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, from 'A'ishah, that she said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would order his bedding to be spread for him facing the qiblah, and when he lay down upon it he would place his right palm under his cheek; then he would murmur – one does not know what he was saying – and when it was the last part of the night he would raise his voice and say: "O Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the Mighty Throne, God of everything and Lord of everything, Revealer of the Torah, the Gospel and the Criterion, Splitter of the seed and the date-stone, I seek refuge in You from the evil of everything You hold by its forelock. O Allah, You are the First who has nothing before You, You are the Last who has nothing after You, You are the Manifest so there is nothing above You, and You are the Hidden so there is nothing beneath You. Settle our debt for us, and enrich us from poverty" [[Musnad Abi Ya'la (8/210).]]

As for al-Sari ibn Isma'il, he is the cousin of al-Sha'bi, and he is very weak, and Allah knows best.

Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi said, at the explanation of this verse: 'Abd ibn Humayd and others narrated to us – the meaning is one – they said: Yunus ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Shaiban ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: al-Hasan narrated to us, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: While the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sitting with his companions, a cloud came over them, and the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do you know what this is?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "This is the 'anan (clouds); these are the water-carriers of the earth, driving it to a people who do not thank Him and do not call upon Him." Then he said: "Do you know what is above you?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "It is the raqi', a protected ceiling, and a surging wave restrained." Then he said: "Do you know how far between you and it?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Between you and it is five hundred years." Then he said: "Do you know what is above that?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Above that is a heaven, the distance between them being a five-hundred-year journey – until he counted seven heavens – between every two heavens is as between the heaven and the earth." Then he said: "Do you know what is above that?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Above that is the Throne, and between it and the heaven is a distance like that between two heavens." Then he said: "Do you know what is beneath you?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "It is the earth." Then he said: "Do you know what is beneath that?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Beneath it is another earth, between them a five-hundred-year journey – until he counted seven earths – between every two earths is a five-hundred-year journey." Then he said: "By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, if you were to lower a rope to the lowest earth, it would descend upon Allah." Then he recited: ﴿He is the First and the Last and the Manifest and the Hidden, and He is Knowing of all things﴾.

Then al-Tirmidhi said: This is a gharib hadith from this route. It is also narrated from Ayyub, Yunus – meaning Ibn 'Ubayd – and 'Ali ibn Zayd, who said: al-Hasan did not hear from Abu Hurayrah. Some scholars explained this hadith, saying: "It descended upon Allah's knowledge, His power and His authority; Allah's knowledge, power and authority are everywhere, while He is upon the Throne, as He described in His Book." End of his words [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3298).]].

Imam Ahmad narrated this hadith from Surayj, from al-Hakam ibn 'Abd al-Malik, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), and mentioned it; in his version the distance between the earths is a seven-hundred-year journey, and he said: "If you were to lower one of you with a rope to the lowest earth, the seventh, it would descend upon Allah." Then he recited: ﴿He is the First and the Last and the Manifest and the Hidden, and He is Knowing of all things﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bazzar narrated it from the hadith of Abu Ja'far al-Razi, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, from Abu Hurayrah... and mentioned the hadith, but Ibn Abi Hatim did not mention its end, which is his saying: "If you were to lower with a rope," rather he said: "until he counted seven earths, between every two earths a five-hundred-year journey," then he recited ﴿He is the First and the Last and the Manifest and the Hidden, and He is Knowing of all things﴾.

Al-Bazzar said: No one narrated it from the Prophet (ﷺ) except Abu Hurayrah.

Ibn Jarir narrated from Bishr, from Yazid, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿He is the First and the Last and the Manifest and the Hidden﴾: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ), while sitting with his companions, a cloud rose over them, and he said: "Do you know what this is?" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (27/124).]] and he mentioned the hadith in the same form as the wording of al-Tirmidhi, except that it is mursal by this route, and perhaps this is the preserved version, and Allah knows best. It has also been narrated from the hadith of Abu Dharr al-Ghifari, may Allah be pleased with him and content him, narrated by al-Bazzar in his Musnad, and by al-Bayhaqi in Kitab al-Asma' wa al-Sifat [[al-Asma' wa al-Sifat by al-Bayhaqi (p. 506), by a route from Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar, from Abu Mu'awiyah, from al-A'mash, from Abu Nasr, from Abu Dharr; and by al-Bayhaqi's route it was narrated by al-Jawzaqani in al-Abatil (1/68), who said: "This is a munkar hadith."]]. But in its chain there is scrutiny, and in its text there is strangeness and repugnance, and Allah, glorified and exalted, knows best.

Ibn Jarir said, at His saying ﴿and of the earth the like of them﴾ [al-Talaq: 12]: Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: Four angels met between the heaven and the earth, and some of them said to others: "Where have you come from?" One of them said: "My Lord, Mighty and Majestic, sent me from the seventh heaven, and I left Him there." Another said: "My Lord, Mighty and Majestic, sent me from the seventh earth, and I left Him there." Another said: "My Lord sent me from the east, and I left Him there." Another said: "My Lord sent me from the west, and I left Him there" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/99).]].

This [hadith] [[addition from M.]] is very strange, and it may be that the first hadith is mawquf upon Qatadah, as is narrated here as his own statement, and Allah knows best.

He gives life and causes death﴾, meaning: He is the Owner who disposes of His creation, so He gives life and causes death, and bestows on whom He wills what He wills. ﴿And He is Competent over all things﴾, meaning: whatever He wills comes to be, and whatever He does not will does not come to be.

* *

His saying: ﴿He is the First and the Last and the Manifest and the Hidden﴾. This is the verse referred to in the hadith of 'Irbad ibn Sariyah, that it is better than a thousand verses.

Abu Dawud said: 'Abbas ibn 'Abd al-'Azim narrated to us, al-Nadr ibn Muhammad narrated to us, 'Ikrimah (i.e., ibn 'Ammar) narrated to us, Abu Zumayl narrated to us, who said: I asked Ibn 'Abbas, "What is something I find in my chest?" He said, "What is it?" I said, "By Allah, I will not speak of it." He said to me, "Is it something of doubt?" – and he laughed – and said, "No one is free of that." He said: until Allah revealed ﴿So if you are in doubt about what We have sent down to you, then ask those who read the Book before you [The truth has certainly come to you from your Lord]﴾ [[addition from M.]] [Yunus: 94]. He said: And he said to me: "When you find something within yourself, say: ﴿He is the First and the Last and the Manifest and the Hidden, and He is Knowing of all things﴾" [[Sunan Abi Dawud no. (5110).]]

The expressions of the exegetes regarding this verse have differed, and their statements number around a dozen.

Al-Bukhari said: Yahya said: "The Manifest over everything in knowledge, and the Hidden over everything in knowledge." [[Sahih al-Bukhari (13/361) "Fath".]]

Our shaykh, the Hafiz al-Mizzi, said: This Yahya is Ibn Ziyad al-Farra', who has a book he named "Ma'ani al-Quran".

Concerning this, there are hadiths. Among them is what Imam Ahmad said: Khalaf ibn al-Walid narrated to us, Ibn 'Ayyash narrated to us, from Suhayl ibn Abi Salih, from his father, from Abu Hurayrah, that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) used to supplicate [[in M: "say"]] at the time of sleep: "O Allah, Lord of the seven heavens, and Lord of the Mighty Throne, our Lord and Lord of all things, Revealer of the Torah, the Gospel and the Criterion, Splitter of the seed and the date-stone, there is no god but You. I seek refuge in You from the evil of everything You hold by its forelock. You are the First, there is nothing before You; and You are the Last, there is nothing after You; and You are the Manifest, there is nothing above You; and You are the Hidden, there is nothing beneath You. Settle our debt for us, and enrich us from poverty" [[al-Musnad (2/404).]]

Muslim also narrated it in his Sahih: Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me, Jarir narrated to us, from Suhayl, who said: Abu Salih used to instruct us, when one of us wished to sleep, to lie on his right side, then say: "O Allah, Lord of the heavens and Lord of the earth and Lord of the Mighty Throne, our Lord and Lord of all things, Splitter of the seed and the date-stone, Revealer of the Torah, the Gospel and the Criterion, I seek refuge in You from the evil of every evil-doer whose forelock You hold. O Allah, You are the First, so there is nothing before You; You are the Last, so there is nothing after You; You are the Manifest, so there is nothing above You; and You are the Hidden, so there is nothing beneath You. Settle our debt for us, and enrich us from poverty."

And he [Abu Salih] would narrate this from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ) [[Sahih Muslim no. (2713).]].

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili also narrated in his Musnad from 'A'ishah, Mother of the Believers, something similar, saying: 'Uqbah narrated to us, Yunus narrated to us, al-Sari ibn Isma'il narrated to us, from al-Sha'bi, from Masruq, from 'A'ishah, that she said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) would order his bedding to be spread for him facing the qiblah, and when he lay down upon it he would place his right palm under his cheek; then he would murmur – one does not know what he was saying – and when it was the last part of the night he would raise his voice and say: "O Allah, Lord of the seven heavens and Lord of the Mighty Throne, God of everything and Lord of everything, Revealer of the Torah, the Gospel and the Criterion, Splitter of the seed and the date-stone, I seek refuge in You from the evil of everything You hold by its forelock. O Allah, You are the First who has nothing before You, You are the Last who has nothing after You, You are the Manifest so there is nothing above You, and You are the Hidden so there is nothing beneath You. Settle our debt for us, and enrich us from poverty" [[Musnad Abi Ya'la (8/210).]]

As for al-Sari ibn Isma'il, he is the cousin of al-Sha'bi, and he is very weak, and Allah knows best.

Abu 'Isa al-Tirmidhi said, at the explanation of this verse: 'Abd ibn Humayd and others narrated to us – the meaning is one – they said: Yunus ibn Muhammad narrated to us, Shaiban ibn 'Abd al-Rahman narrated to us, from Qatadah, who said: al-Hasan narrated to us, from Abu Hurayrah, who said: While the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) was sitting with his companions, a cloud came over them, and the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Do you know what this is?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "This is the 'anan (clouds); these are the water-carriers of the earth, driving it to a people who do not thank Him and do not call upon Him." Then he said: "Do you know what is above you?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "It is the raqi', a protected ceiling, and a surging wave restrained." Then he said: "Do you know how far between you and it?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Between you and it is five hundred years." Then he said: "Do you know what is above that?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Above that is a heaven, the distance between them being a five-hundred-year journey – until he counted seven heavens – between every two heavens is as between the heaven and the earth." Then he said: "Do you know what is above that?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Above that is the Throne, and between it and the heaven is a distance like that between two heavens." Then he said: "Do you know what is beneath you?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "It is the earth." Then he said: "Do you know what is beneath that?" They said: "Allah and His Messenger know best." He said: "Beneath it is another earth, between them a five-hundred-year journey – until he counted seven earths – between every two earths is a five-hundred-year journey." Then he said: "By Him in whose hand is the soul of Muhammad, if you were to lower a rope to the lowest earth, it would descend upon Allah." Then he recited: ﴿He is the First and the Last and the Manifest and the Hidden, and He is Knowing of all things﴾.

Then al-Tirmidhi said: This is a gharib hadith from this route. It is also narrated from Ayyub, Yunus – meaning Ibn 'Ubayd – and 'Ali ibn Zayd, who said: al-Hasan did not hear from Abu Hurayrah. Some scholars explained this hadith, saying: "It descended upon Allah's knowledge, His power and His authority; Allah's knowledge, power and authority are everywhere, while He is upon the Throne, as He described in His Book." End of his words [[Sunan al-Tirmidhi no. (3298).]].

Imam Ahmad narrated this hadith from Surayj, from al-Hakam ibn 'Abd al-Malik, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Prophet (ﷺ), and mentioned it; in his version the distance between the earths is a seven-hundred-year journey, and he said: "If you were to lower one of you with a rope to the lowest earth, the seventh, it would descend upon Allah." Then he recited: ﴿He is the First and the Last and the Manifest and the Hidden, and He is Knowing of all things﴾.

Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bazzar narrated it from the hadith of Abu Ja'far al-Razi, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, from Abu Hurayrah... and mentioned the hadith, but Ibn Abi Hatim did not mention its end, which is his saying: "If you were to lower with a rope," rather he said: "until he counted seven earths, between every two earths a five-hundred-year journey," then he recited ﴿He is the First and the Last and the Manifest and the Hidden, and He is Knowing of all things﴾.

Al-Bazzar said: No one narrated it from the Prophet (ﷺ) except Abu Hurayrah.

Ibn Jarir narrated from Bishr, from Yazid, from Sa'id, from Qatadah, concerning ﴿He is the First and the Last and the Manifest and the Hidden﴾: It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ), while sitting with his companions, a cloud rose over them, and he said: "Do you know what this is?" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (27/124).]] and he mentioned the hadith in the same form as the wording of al-Tirmidhi, except that it is mursal by this route, and perhaps this is the preserved version, and Allah knows best. It has also been narrated from the hadith of Abu Dharr al-Ghifari, may Allah be pleased with him and content him, narrated by al-Bazzar in his Musnad, and by al-Bayhaqi in Kitab al-Asma' wa al-Sifat [[al-Asma' wa al-Sifat by al-Bayhaqi (p. 506), by a route from Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Jabbar, from Abu Mu'awiyah, from al-A'mash, from Abu Nasr, from Abu Dharr; and by al-Bayhaqi's route it was narrated by al-Jawzaqani in al-Abatil (1/68), who said: "This is a munkar hadith."]]. But in its chain there is scrutiny, and in its text there is strangeness and repugnance, and Allah, glorified and exalted, knows best.

Ibn Jarir said, at His saying ﴿and of the earth the like of them﴾ [al-Talaq: 12]: Ibn 'Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Ibn Thawr narrated to us, from Ma'mar, from Qatadah, who said: Four angels met between the heaven and the earth, and some of them said to others: "Where have you come from?" One of them said: "My Lord, Mighty and Majestic, sent me from the seventh heaven, and I left Him there." Another said: "My Lord, Mighty and Majestic, sent me from the seventh earth, and I left Him there." Another said: "My Lord sent me from the east, and I left Him there." Another said: "My Lord sent me from the west, and I left Him there" [[Tafsir al-Tabari (28/99).]].

This [hadith] [[addition from M.]] is very strange, and it may be that the first hadith is mawquf upon Qatadah, as is narrated here as his own statement, and Allah knows best.

Ibn Kathir's commentary on Surah 57, verses 4–6:

Allah informs us that He created the heavens and the earth and what is between them in six days. Then He informed us that He istawa (rose over/settled upon) the Throne after creating them. The discussion of this verse and its like has already been given in Surah al-A'raf [[At the commentary on verse 54.]], in a way that makes repeating it here unnecessary.

﴿He knows what enters the earth﴾, meaning He knows the number of what enters it of seed and rain, ﴿and what comes out of it﴾ of crops, plants and fruits. As He said: ﴿With Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them but He. He knows what is on the land and in the sea. No leaf falls but that He knows it, nor is there a grain in the darknesses of the earth, nor anything moist or dry, but that it is in a clear Book﴾ [al-An'am: 59].

* *

His saying: ﴿and what descends from the sky﴾, meaning of rain, snow and hail, and of decrees and commands, along with the noble angels. It has already been mentioned in Surah al-Baqarah that no drop descends from the sky except that with it is an angel who places it in the place Allah commands, wherever He wills, may He be exalted.

* *

His saying: ﴿and what ascends into it﴾, meaning of the angels and deeds, as has come in the Sahih: "The deed of the night is raised up to Him before the deed of the day, and the deed of the day before the deed of the night" [[Sahih Muslim, no. (179), from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him.]].

* *

His saying: ﴿And He is with you wherever you are, and Allah is Seeing of what you do﴾, meaning: He is Watchful over you and Witness to your deeds wherever you are, and wherever you may be, on land or at sea, at night or by day, in houses or in deserts. All are equal in His knowledge, and under His sight and hearing. He hears your speech, sees your place, and knows your secrets and private conversations. As He said: ﴿Verily, they fold their breasts to hide from Him. Unquestionably, when they cover themselves with their garments, He knows what they conceal and what they reveal. Indeed, He is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾ [Hud: 5]. And He said: ﴿It is the same whether one of you conceals speech or speaks openly, whether one hides by night or goes forth by day﴾ [al-Ra'd: 10]. There is no deity except Him, and no lord besides Him.

It is established in the Sahih that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Jibril, when he asked him about ihsan (excellence): "That you worship Allah as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, then indeed He sees you."

Al-Hafiz (the memorizer of hadith, a title of distinction) Abu Bakr al-Isma'ili narrated from the hadith of Nasr ibn Khuzaymah ibn Junadah ibn Mahfuz ibn 'Alqamah, who said: my father related to me, from Nasr ibn 'Alqamah, from his brother, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'A'idh, who said: 'Umar said: A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "Give me a word to live by." He said: "Be shy before Allah as you would be shy before a righteous man of your clan, who does not leave you."

[[The author mentioned it in the Musnad of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab (2/609) via al-Isma'ili, and said: "Its isnad is gharib (strange/unusual). In the hadith of qadar (divine decree) there is: 'If you do not see Him, then indeed He sees you.' It has a witness from the hadith of Sa'id ibn Yazid, from a paternal cousin of his, who said: 'I said: O Messenger of Allah, advise me.' He said: 'Be shy before Allah as you are shy before the righteous man of your people.' Recorded by Mujshil in Tarikh Wasit (p. 209)."]]

This is a gharib hadith. Abu Nu'aym narrated from the hadith of 'Abd Allah ibn Mu'awiyah al-Ghadiri, marfu' (traced to the Prophet ﷺ): "Whoever does three things has tasted faith: whoever worships Allah alone, gives the zakat of his wealth willingly and with a good soul every year, and does not give the decrepit, the diseased, or the mean and sickly animals, but gives from the middle of your wealth, and purifies himself." A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is a person's purification of himself?" He said: "That he knows that Allah is with him wherever he is."

[[Al-Bayhaqi narrated it in al-Sunan al-Kubra (4/96) via al-Zubaydi from Yahya ibn Jabir, that 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Jubayr told him that his father told him that 'Abd Allah ibn Mu'awiyah al-Ghadiri (narrated) it. Abu Dawud narrated it via al-Zubaydi from Yahya ibn Jabir, from Jubayr ibn Nufayr, similar to it. The first is more authentic.]]

Nu'aym ibn Hammad, may Allah have mercy on him, said: Uthman ibn Sa'id ibn Kathir ibn Dinar al-Himsi related to us, from Muhammad ibn Muhajir, from 'Urwah ibn Ruwaym, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn Ghanm, from 'Ubadah ibn al-Samit, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Indeed the best of faith is that you know that Allah is with you wherever you are." Gharib.

[[Al-Tabarani narrated it in al-Mu'jam al-Awsat, no. (47) "Majma' al-Bahrayn," from Mutallib, from Nu'aym ibn Hammad with it, and said: "Uthman alone narrated it." Abu Nu'aym narrated it in al-Hilyah (6/124) from al-Tabarani, from Yahya ibn Uthman, from Nu'aym ibn Hammad with it, and said: "Gharib from the hadith of 'Urwah; we did not write it except from the hadith of Muhammad ibn Muhajir." Al-Haythami did not identify Uthman ibn Sa'id in Majma' al-Zawa'id (1/60). Ibn Abi Hatim mentioned him in al-Jarh wa al-Ta'dil (6/152) and transmitted from Yahya ibn Ma'in that he is thiqah (trustworthy).]]

Imam Ahmad used to recite these two verses:

When you are alone for a time, do not say, "I am alone,"
but say, "A watcher is upon me."

And do not think that Allah is heedless for an hour,
nor that what is hidden from Him is ever absent.

* *

His saying: ﴿To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and to Allah all matters are returned﴾, meaning: He is the Owner of this world and the Hereafter, as He said: ﴿And indeed, to Us belong the Hereafter and the first life﴾ [al-Layl: 13]. He is the One praised for that, as He said: ﴿He is Allah; there is no deity but Him. To Him belongs praise in the first life and the Hereafter﴾ [al-Qasas: 70]. And He said: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and to Him belongs praise in the Hereafter. And He is the Wise, the All-Aware﴾ [Saba': 1]. So all that is in the heavens and the earth belongs to Him, and their inhabitants are servants, slaves, humbled before Him, as He said: ﴿There is none in the heavens and the earth but that he comes to the Most Merciful as a servant. He has enumerated them and counted them with an exact counting. And each of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone﴾ [Maryam: 93–95]. Therefore He said: ﴿And to Allah all matters are returned﴾, meaning: the return is to Him on the Day of Resurrection, and He judges His creation as He wills. He is the Just who does not oppress, and does not wrong even the weight of an atom. Rather, if any of them does a single good deed, He multiplies it tenfold, ﴿and gives from Himself a great reward﴾ [al-Nisa': 40]. As Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We will set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, and no soul will be wronged in anything. And if it is the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it. And sufficient are We as reckoners﴾ [al-Anbiya': 47].

* *

His saying: ﴿He causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night﴾, meaning: He is the One who directs creation. He alternates night and day and determines them by His wisdom as He wills. Sometimes He lengthens the night and shortens the day, sometimes the reverse, and sometimes He makes them equal. Sometimes the season is winter, then spring, then summer, then autumn. All of that is by His wisdom and His decree for what He wills for His creation. ﴿And He is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾, meaning: He knows the secrets, however subtle, and however hidden.

As He said: ﴿With Him are the keys of the unseen; none knows them but He. He knows what is on the land and in the sea. No leaf falls but that He knows it, nor is there a grain in the darknesses of the earth, nor anything moist or dry, but that it is in a clear Book﴾ [al-An'am: 59].

* *

His saying: ﴿and what descends from the sky﴾, meaning of rain, snow and hail, and of decrees and commands, along with the noble angels. It has already been mentioned in Surah al-Baqarah that no drop descends from the sky except that with it is an angel who places it in the place Allah commands, wherever He wills, may He be exalted.

* *

His saying: ﴿and what ascends into it﴾, meaning of the angels and deeds, as has come in the Sahih: "The deed of the night is raised up to Him before the deed of the day, and the deed of the day before the deed of the night" [[Sahih Muslim, no. (179), from the hadith of Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, may Allah be pleased with him.]].

* *

His saying: ﴿And He is with you wherever you are, and Allah is Seeing of what you do﴾, meaning: He is Watchful over you and Witness to your deeds wherever you are, and wherever you may be, on land or at sea, at night or by day, in houses or in deserts. All are equal in His knowledge, and under His sight and hearing. He hears your speech, sees your place, and knows your secrets and private conversations. As He said: ﴿Verily, they fold their breasts to hide from Him. Unquestionably, when they cover themselves with their garments, He knows what they conceal and what they reveal. Indeed, He is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾ [Hud: 5]. And He said: ﴿It is the same whether one of you conceals speech or speaks openly, whether one hides by night or goes forth by day﴾ [al-Ra'd: 10]. There is no deity except Him, and no lord besides Him.

It is established in the Sahih that the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said to Jibril, when he asked him about ihsan (excellence): "That you worship Allah as if you see Him, and if you do not see Him, then indeed He sees you."

Al-Hafiz (the memorizer of hadith, a title of distinction) Abu Bakr al-Isma'ili narrated from the hadith of Nasr ibn Khuzaymah ibn Junadah ibn Mahfuz ibn 'Alqamah, who said: my father related to me, from Nasr ibn 'Alqamah, from his brother, from 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'A'idh, who said: 'Umar said: A man came to the Prophet (ﷺ) and said: "Give me a word to live by." He said: "Be shy before Allah as you would be shy before a righteous man of your clan, who does not leave you."

A man said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is a person's purification of himself?" He said: "That he knows that Allah is with him wherever he is."

Imam Ahmad used to recite these two verses:

When you are alone for a time, do not say, "I am alone,"
but say, "A watcher is upon me."

And do not think that Allah is heedless for an hour,
nor that what is hidden from Him is ever absent.

* *

His saying: ﴿To Him belongs the dominion of the heavens and the earth, and to Allah all matters are returned﴾, meaning: He is the Owner of this world and the Hereafter, as He said: ﴿And indeed, to Us belong the Hereafter and the first life﴾ [al-Layl: 13]. He is the One praised for that, as He said: ﴿He is Allah; there is no deity but Him. To Him belongs praise in the first life and the Hereafter﴾ [al-Qasas: 70]. And He said: ﴿All praise is due to Allah, to whom belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth, and to Him belongs praise in the Hereafter. And He is the Wise, the All-Aware﴾ [Saba': 1]. So all that is in the heavens and the earth belongs to Him, and their inhabitants are servants, slaves, humbled before Him, as He said: ﴿There is none in the heavens and the earth but that he comes to the Most Merciful as a servant. He has enumerated them and counted them with an exact counting. And each of them will come to Him on the Day of Resurrection alone﴾ [Maryam: 93–95]. Therefore He said: ﴿And to Allah all matters are returned﴾, meaning: the return is to Him on the Day of Resurrection, and He judges His creation as He wills. He is the Just who does not oppress, and does not wrong even the weight of an atom. Rather, if any of them does a single good deed, He multiplies it tenfold, ﴿and gives from Himself a great reward﴾ [al-Nisa': 40]. As Allah, the Exalted, said: ﴿And We will set up the scales of justice for the Day of Resurrection, and no soul will be wronged in anything. And if it is the weight of a mustard seed, We will bring it. And sufficient are We as reckoners﴾ [al-Anbiya': 47].

* *

His saying: ﴿He causes the night to enter into the day and causes the day to enter into the night﴾, meaning: He is the One who directs creation. He alternates night and day and determines them by His wisdom as He wills. Sometimes He lengthens the night and shortens the day, sometimes the reverse, and sometimes He makes them equal. Sometimes the season is winter, then spring, then summer, then autumn. All of that is by His wisdom and His decree for what He wills for His creation. ﴿And He is Knowing of what is within the breasts﴾, meaning: He knows the secrets, however subtle, and however hidden.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 57, verses 7–11 (part 1 of 2):

He, exalted is He, commanded belief in Him and in His Messenger in the most perfect manner, and persistence, steadfastness and continuity in that. He urged spending from that in which He has made you successors (mustakhlafin), meaning from what is with you by way of 'ariyah (a loan, something held in trust and not owned absolutely). For it was in the hands of those before you, and then passed to you. So He guided them to using the wealth in which He had made them successors in His obedience. If they do not do so, He will call them to account for it and punish them for abandoning their obligations concerning it.
* *
His saying: ﴿from that in which He has made you successors﴾ contains an indication that you will be left behind by it. Perhaps your heir will obey Allah in it, and he will then be happier with what Allah has bestowed upon him than you were with it. Or he will disobey Allah in it, and you will have contributed to helping him in sin and transgression.
Imam Ahmad said: Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to us, Shu'bah narrated to us, I heard Qatadah narrating, from Mutarrif, that is Ibn 'Abd Allah ibn al-Shikhkhir, from his father, who said: I came to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ while he was reciting: ﴿Rivalry in worldly increase distracts you﴾ [al-Takathur: 1]. He said: "The son of Adam says, 'My wealth, my wealth!' Do you have from your wealth anything but what you have eaten and consumed, or what you have worn and worn out, or what you have given in charity and sent forward?"
Muslim also narrated it through the hadith of Shu'bah, with the same chain, and added: "And whatever is other than that will perish, and he will leave it to the people." [Al-Musnad (4/24) and Sahih Muslim, no. 2958.]
* *
His saying: ﴿So those of you who believe and spend, for them is a great reward﴾ is an encouragement to belief and to spending in obedience.
Then He said: ﴿And what is wrong with you that you do not believe in Allah, while the Messenger calls you to believe in your Lord?﴾ That is: what prevents you from believing while the Messenger is among you, calling you to that and making clear to you the proofs and evidences for the truth of what he has brought you? We have related in the hadith, by several routes, at the beginning of the explanation of the "Book of Faith" in Sahih al-Bukhari, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said one day to his companions: "Which of the believers do you consider most wondrous in faith?" They said: "The angels." He said: "And why would they not believe, when they are in the presence of their Lord?" They said: "Then the prophets." He said: "And why would they not believe, when revelation descends upon them?" They said: "Then us?" He said: "And what is wrong with you that you do not believe, when I am among you? Rather, the most wondrous of the believers in faith are a people who will come after you, who will find pages (suhuf) and will believe in what is in them." [This hadith's takhrij was already mentioned in the tafsir of verse 3 of surah al-Baqarah.]
We have already mentioned a portion of this at the beginning of surah al-Baqarah, at His saying: ﴿Who believe in the unseen﴾ [al-Baqarah: 3].
* *
His saying: ﴿And He has taken your covenant﴾ is like His saying: ﴿And remember the favour of Allah upon you and His covenant with which He bound you when you said, "We hear and we obey"﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 7]. What is meant is the pledge of allegiance (bay'ah) to the Messenger ﷺ.
Ibn Jarir claimed that what is meant by that is the covenant taken from them in the loins of Adam, and this is the view of Mujahid. And Allah knows best.
* *
His saying: ﴿It is He who sends down upon His servant clear verses﴾ means: clear proofs, manifest evidences and decisive arguments, ﴿to bring you out from darknesses into light﴾ means: from the darkness of ignorance, disbelief and conflicting opinions into the light of guidance, certainty and faith. ﴿And indeed, Allah is to you Kind and Merciful﴾ means: in His sending down the books and sending the messengers to guide people, and removing the impediments and dispelling doubts.
When He had first commanded them to believe and to spend, then urged them to believe, and made clear that He had removed the obstacles to it from them, He urged them also to spend. So He said: ﴿And what is wrong with you that you do not spend in the way of Allah, when to Allah belongs the heritage of the heavens and the earth?﴾ That is: spend, and do not fear poverty and want, for He in whose way you spend is the owner of the heavens and the earth, and the keys of both are in His hand, and their treasuries are with Him, and He is the Lord of the Throne with all that it encompasses. He is the one who said: ﴿And whatever you spend of anything, He will replace it, and He is the best of providers﴾ [Saba': 39], and He said: ﴿What is with you will be exhausted, but what is with Allah remains﴾ [al-Nahl: 96]. So whoever trusts in Allah spends, and does not fear poverty from the Lord of the Throne, and knows that Allah will replace it for him.
* *
His saying: ﴿Not equal among you are those who spent and fought before the conquest﴾ means: this is not equal to one who did not do as he did. That is because before the conquest of Makkah the situation was severe, and at that time none believed except the sincere (siddiqun). But after the conquest, Islam became manifest in a great way, and people entered the religion of Allah in multitudes. For this reason He said: ﴿Those are greater in rank than those who spent afterward and fought. But to each Allah has promised the best.﴾
The majority hold that what is meant here by "the conquest" is the conquest of Makkah. Al-Sha'bi and others said that what is meant here by the conquest is the Treaty of al-Hudaybiyah. This view may be supported by what Imam Ahmad said:
Ahmad ibn 'Abd al-Malik narrated to us, Zuhayr narrated to us, Humayd al-Tawil narrated to us, from Anas, who said: There was an exchange of words between Khalid ibn al-Walid and 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf. Khalid said to 'Abd al-Rahman: "Do you exalt yourselves over us with days you preceded us in?" It reached us that this was mentioned to the Prophet ﷺ, and he said: "Leave my companions to me. By Him in whose hand is my soul, if you were to spend the like of Uhud, or the like of the mountains, in gold, you would not reach their deeds." [Al-Musnad (3/266).]
It is known that the conversion of Khalid ibn al-Walid, the one addressed by this speech, took place between the Treaty of al-Hudaybiyah and the conquest of Makkah. This dispute between them was about the Banu Jadhimah, to whom the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sent Khalid ibn al-Walid after the conquest. They began saying: "Sabana, sabana" (we have changed religion, we have changed religion), and did not properly say "Aslamna" (we have submitted). So Khalid ordered them to be killed, and those among them who had been taken captive to be killed. 'Abd al-Rahman ibn 'Awf, 'Abd Allah ibn 'Umar and others opposed him. Khalid and 'Abd al-Rahman then disputed about that matter. [Related by al-Bukhari in his Sahih, no. 7189, from the hadith of Ibn 'Umar, may Allah be pleased with him.]
What is in the Sahih from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ is that he said: "Do not revile my companions. By Him in whose hand is my soul, if one of you were to spend the like of Uhud in gold, it would not reach a mudd of one of them, nor half of it." [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3673, and Sahih Muslim, no. 2541, from the hadith of Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may Allah be pleased with him.]
Ibn Jarir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated, from the hadith of Ibn Wahb: Hisham ibn Sa'd informed us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that he said: "We went out with the Messenger of Allah ﷺ in the year of al-Hudaybiyah, until when we were at 'Usfan, the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: 'Soon there will come a people whom you will consider your deeds small in comparison with theirs.' We said: 'Who are they, O Messenger of Allah? Quraysh?' He said: 'No, but the people of Yemen; they are more tender of heart and softer in hearts.' We said: 'Are they better than us, O Messenger of Allah?' He said: 'If one of them had a mountain of gold and spent it, he would not attain a mudd of one of you, nor half of it. Indeed this is the excellence between us and the people: ﴿Not equal among you are those who spent and fought before the conquest. Those are greater in rank than those who spent afterward and fought. But to each Allah has promised the best. And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾'" [Tafsir al-Tabari (27/127).]
This hadith is strange in this form. What is in the two Sahihs, from the transmission of a group, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id (mentioning the Kharijites): "You will consider your prayer small in comparison with their prayer, and your fasting in comparison with their fasting; they will pass through the religion as an arrow passes through its target," is the hadith [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 6931, and Sahih Muslim, no. 4601]. However, Ibn Jarir narrated this hadith by another route, saying:
Ibn al-Barqi narrated to me, Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far informed us, Zayd ibn Aslam informed me, from Abu Sa'id al-Tammar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Soon there will come a people whom you will consider your deeds small in comparison with theirs." We said: "Who are they, O Messenger of Allah? Quraysh?" He said: "No, but the people of Yemen, because they are more tender of heart and softer in hearts." And he pointed with his hand toward Yemen and said: "They are the people of Yemen. Verily faith is Yamani, and wisdom is Yamani." We said: "O Messenger of Allah, are they better than us?" He said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, if one of them had a mountain of gold that he spent, he would not attain a mudd of one of you, nor half of it." Then he gathered his fingers and extended his little finger, and said: "Indeed this is the excellence between us and the people: ﴿Not equal among you are those who spent and fought before the conquest. Those are greater in rank than those who spent afterward and fought. But to each Allah has promised the best. And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾"" [Addition from M and A.] [Tafsir al-Tabari (17/127).]
This context contains no mention of al-Hudaybiyah. If that is preserved as already stated, it is possible that the verse was revealed before the conquest, as news of what would come after it, as in His saying in surah al-Muzzammil, which is Meccan and among the first things revealed: ﴿And others fighting in the way of Allah﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 20]. So it is good tidings of what is to come, and likewise this one. And Allah knows best.
* *
His saying: ﴿But to each Allah has promised the best﴾ means those who spent before the conquest and after it. All of them have reward for what they did, although there is variation among them in the degrees of reward, as He said: ﴿Not equal are those who sit [at home] among the believers, other than the disabled, and those who strive in the way of Allah with their wealth and their lives. Allah has preferred those who strive with their wealth and lives over those who sit [at home] by a degree. But to all Allah has promised the best. And Allah has preferred the strivers over those who sit [at home] with a great reward﴾ [al-Nisa': 95]. Likewise is the hadith in the Sahih: "The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, and there is good in both." [Sahih Muslim, no. 2664, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.] He mentioned this only so that the one side is not discounted by praising the first without the other, lest someone suppose that the other is being blamed. Therefore He followed the praise of the other with commendation of him, while giving preference to the first over him. For this reason He said: ﴿And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾ That is: by His knowledge He differentiated between the reward of one who spent before the conquest and fought, and one who did so afterward. And this was only because of His knowledge of the first one's intention and his complete sincerity, and his spending in a state of hardship, scarcity and constraint. In the hadith: "A dirham has outstripped one hundred thousand" [Related by al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan (5/59), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]. There is no doubt among the people of faith that al-Siddiq Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, has the greatest share of this verse, for he is the chief of all who acted upon it among the nations of the prophets. He spent all his wealth seeking the Face of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and no one had a favour upon him for which he needed to repay.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 57, verses 7–11 (part 2 of 2):

Abu Muhammad al-Husayn ibn Mas'ud al-Baghawi said, while explaining this verse: Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Shurayhi informed us [[In manuscript A: "al-Shar'i".]] Abu Ishaq Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Tha'labi informed us. 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid ibn Muhammad informed us. Ahmad ibn Ishaq ibn Ayyub informed us. Muhammad ibn Yunus narrated to us. Al-'Ala' ibn 'Amr al-Shaybani narrated to us. Abu Ishaq al-Fazari narrated to us. Sufyan ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Adam ibn 'Ali, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: "I was with the Prophet (ﷺ), and with him was Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, and he was wearing a cloak which he had fastened at his chest with a thorn. Then Jibril descended and said: 'Why do I see Abu Bakr wearing a cloak which he has fastened at his chest with a thorn?' The Prophet said: 'He spent his wealth on me before the Conquest.' [Jibril] said: 'Indeed Allah says: Convey to him the greeting of peace, and say to him: Are you pleased with Me in this poverty of yours, or displeased?' The Messenger of Allah said: 'O Abu Bakr, indeed Allah conveys to you the greeting of peace and says to you: Are you pleased with Me in this poverty of yours, or displeased?' Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said: 'Would I be displeased with my Lord, Mighty and Majestic? Indeed I am pleased with my Lord, [I am pleased with my Lord]'" [[Ma'alim al-Tanzil by al-Baghawi (8/34), and in it: "Indeed I am pleased with my Lord" twice. Its weakness is that it contains al-'Ala' ibn 'Amr. Ibn Hibban said: "Abu Ishaq al-Fazari narrates strange reports; it is not permissible to argue with him at all," and he then cited the hadith.]]

This hadith is weak in its chain from this route.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Who is it that will lend to Allah a goodly loan﴾. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said: it is spending in the way of Allah. It was also said: it is providing for one's dependents. The correct view is that it is more general than that: whoever spends in the way of Allah with a sincere intention and a truthful resolve enters into the generality of this verse. For this reason He said: ﴿Who is it that will lend to Allah a goodly loan, so that He may multiply it for him﴾, as He said in the other verse: ﴿many times over. And Allah withholds and extends [provision], and to Him you will be returned﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 245] [[In manuscripts A, M, and H: "many times over, and He has a noble reward," which is an error; what we have established is the correct reading.]] That is: a beautiful reward and a dazzling provision, which is Paradise, on the Day of Resurrection.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah narrated to us, Khalaf ibn Khalifah narrated to us, from Humayd al-A'raj, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿Who is it that will lend to Allah a goodly loan, so that He may multiply it for him﴾, Abu al-Dahdah al-Ansari said: "O Messenger of Allah, does Allah really want a loan from us?" He said: "Yes, O Abu al-Dahdah." He said: "Show me your hand, O Messenger of Allah." So he gave him his hand. [Abu al-Dahdah] said: "Indeed I have lent to my Lord my orchard" — he had an orchard in which there were six hundred palm trees, and Umm al-Dahdah and her children were in it. Then Abu al-Dahdah came and called out: "O Umm al-Dahdah!" She said: "At your service." He said: "Come out, for I have lent it to my Lord, Mighty and Majestic." — and in another narration: she said to him: "Your sale has profited, O Abu al-Dahdah," and she carried out her goods and her children from it. And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "How many a thick-clustered palm there is in Paradise for Abu al-Dahdah!" And in another wording: "How many a palm tree whose roots are hanging with pearls and rubies belongs to Abu al-Dahdah in Paradise!" [[Abu Ya'la also narrated it in his Musnad (8/404) from Muhriz ibn 'Awn, from Khalaf ibn Khalifah with the same chain. Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar weakened it in al-Matalib al-'Aliyah, no. (4080), as mentioned by the esteemed editor Husayn Asad.]]

What is in the two Sahihs, from the transmission of a group, from 'Ata' ibn Yasar, from Abu Sa'id (mentioning the Kharijites): "You will consider your prayer small in comparison with their prayer, and your fasting in comparison with their fasting; they will pass through the religion as an arrow passes through its target," is the hadith [Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 6931, and Sahih Muslim, no. 4601]. However, Ibn Jarir narrated this hadith by another route, saying:
Ibn al-Barqi narrated to me, Ibn Abi Maryam narrated to us, Muhammad ibn Ja'far informed us, Zayd ibn Aslam informed me, from Abu Sa'id al-Tammar, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Soon there will come a people whom you will consider your deeds small in comparison with theirs." We said: "Who are they, O Messenger of Allah? Quraysh?" He said: "No, but the people of Yemen, because they are more tender of heart and softer in hearts." And he pointed with his hand toward Yemen and said: "They are the people of Yemen. Verily faith is Yamani, and wisdom is Yamani." We said: "O Messenger of Allah, are they better than us?" He said: "By Him in whose hand is my soul, if one of them had a mountain of gold that he spent, he would not attain a mudd of one of you, nor half of it." Then he gathered his fingers and extended his little finger, and said: "Indeed this is the excellence between us and the people: ﴿Not equal among you are those who spent and fought before the conquest. Those are greater in rank than those who spent afterward and fought. But to each Allah has promised the best. And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾"" [Addition from M and A.] [Tafsir al-Tabari (17/127).]
This context contains no mention of al-Hudaybiyah. If that is preserved as already stated, it is possible that the verse was revealed before the conquest, as news of what would come after it, as in His saying in surah al-Muzzammil, which is Meccan and among the first things revealed: ﴿And others fighting in the way of Allah﴾ [al-Muzzammil: 20]. So it is good tidings of what is to come, and likewise this one. And Allah knows best.
* *
His saying: ﴿But to each Allah has promised the best﴾ means those who spent before the conquest and after it. All of them have reward for what they did, although there is variation among them in the degrees of reward, as He said: ﴿Not equal are those who sit [at home] among the believers, other than the disabled, and those who strive in the way of Allah with their wealth and their lives. Allah has preferred those who strive with their wealth and lives over those who sit [at home] by a degree. But to all Allah has promised the best. And Allah has preferred the strivers over those who sit [at home] with a great reward﴾ [al-Nisa': 95]. Likewise is the hadith in the Sahih: "The strong believer is better and more beloved to Allah than the weak believer, and there is good in both." [Sahih Muslim, no. 2664, from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.] He mentioned this only so that the one side is not discounted by praising the first without the other, lest someone suppose that the other is being blamed. Therefore He followed the praise of the other with commendation of him, while giving preference to the first over him. For this reason He said: ﴿And Allah is Acquainted with what you do.﴾ That is: by His knowledge He differentiated between the reward of one who spent before the conquest and fought, and one who did so afterward. And this was only because of His knowledge of the first one's intention and his complete sincerity, and his spending in a state of hardship, scarcity and constraint. In the hadith: "A dirham has outstripped one hundred thousand" [Related by al-Nasa'i in al-Sunan (5/59), from the hadith of Abu Hurayrah, may Allah be pleased with him.]. There is no doubt among the people of faith that al-Siddiq Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, has the greatest share of this verse, for he is the chief of all who acted upon it among the nations of the prophets. He spent all his wealth seeking the Face of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, and no one had a favour upon him for which he needed to repay.

Commentary of Ibn Kathir (Tafsir al-Quran al-'Azim) on surah 57, verses 7–11 (part 2 of 2):

Abu Muhammad al-Husayn ibn Mas'ud al-Baghawi said, while explaining this verse: Ahmad ibn Ibrahim al-Shurayhi informed us [[In manuscript A: "al-Shar'i".]] Abu Ishaq Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Ibrahim al-Tha'labi informed us. 'Abd Allah ibn Hamid ibn Muhammad informed us. Ahmad ibn Ishaq ibn Ayyub informed us. Muhammad ibn Yunus narrated to us. Al-'Ala' ibn 'Amr al-Shaybani narrated to us. Abu Ishaq al-Fazari narrated to us. Sufyan ibn Sa'id narrated to us, from Adam ibn 'Ali, from Ibn 'Umar, who said: "I was with the Prophet (ﷺ), and with him was Abu Bakr al-Siddiq, and he was wearing a cloak which he had fastened at his chest with a thorn. Then Jibril descended and said: 'Why do I see Abu Bakr wearing a cloak which he has fastened at his chest with a thorn?' The Prophet said: 'He spent his wealth on me before the Conquest.' [Jibril] said: 'Indeed Allah says: Convey to him the greeting of peace, and say to him: Are you pleased with Me in this poverty of yours, or displeased?' The Messenger of Allah said: 'O Abu Bakr, indeed Allah conveys to you the greeting of peace and says to you: Are you pleased with Me in this poverty of yours, or displeased?' Abu Bakr, may Allah be pleased with him, said: 'Would I be displeased with my Lord, Mighty and Majestic? Indeed I am pleased with my Lord, [I am pleased with my Lord]'" [[Ma'alim al-Tanzil by al-Baghawi (8/34), and in it: "Indeed I am pleased with my Lord" twice. Its weakness is that it contains al-'Ala' ibn 'Amr. Ibn Hibban said: "Abu Ishaq al-Fazari narrates strange reports; it is not permissible to argue with him at all," and he then cited the hadith.]]

This hadith is weak in its chain from this route.

* *

And His saying: ﴿Who is it that will lend to Allah a goodly loan﴾. 'Umar ibn al-Khattab said: it is spending in the way of Allah. It was also said: it is providing for one's dependents. The correct view is that it is more general than that: whoever spends in the way of Allah with a sincere intention and a truthful resolve enters into the generality of this verse. For this reason He said: ﴿Who is it that will lend to Allah a goodly loan, so that He may multiply it for him﴾, as He said in the other verse: ﴿many times over. And Allah withholds and extends [provision], and to Him you will be returned﴾ [Al-Baqarah: 245] [[In manuscripts A, M, and H: "many times over, and He has a noble reward," which is an error; what we have established is the correct reading.]] That is: a beautiful reward and a dazzling provision, which is Paradise, on the Day of Resurrection.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: al-Hasan ibn 'Arafah narrated to us, Khalaf ibn Khalifah narrated to us, from Humayd al-A'raj, from 'Abd Allah ibn al-Harith, from 'Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, who said: When this verse was revealed: ﴿Who is it that will lend to Allah a goodly loan, so that He may multiply it for him﴾, Abu al-Dahdah al-Ansari said: "O Messenger of Allah, does Allah really want a loan from us?" He said: "Yes, O Abu al-Dahdah." He said: "Show me your hand, O Messenger of Allah." So he gave him his hand. [Abu al-Dahdah] said: "Indeed I have lent to my Lord my orchard" — he had an orchard in which there were six hundred palm trees, and Umm al-Dahdah and her children were in it. Then Abu al-Dahdah came and called out: "O Umm al-Dahdah!" She said: "At your service." He said: "Come out, for I have lent it to my Lord, Mighty and Majestic." — and in another narration: she said to him: "Your sale has profited, O Abu al-Dahdah," and she carried out her goods and her children from it. And the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "How many a thick-clustered palm there is in Paradise for Abu al-Dahdah!" And in another wording: "How many a palm tree whose roots are hanging with pearls and rubies belongs to Abu al-Dahdah in Paradise!" [[Abu Ya'la also narrated it in his Musnad (8/404) from Muhriz ibn 'Awn, from Khalaf ibn Khalifah with the same chain. Al-Hafiz Ibn Hajar weakened it in al-Matalib al-'Aliyah, no. (4080), as mentioned by the esteemed editor Husayn Asad.]]

Among them is one whose light is like a mountain, and among them is one whose light is like a palm tree, and among them is one whose light is like a standing man. The least of them in light is one whose light is on his big toe, flaring up once and going out once." Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Jarir narrated it. [The Mss. has "that he" (anna-hum) and "and it goes out another time" (wa-yutfa akhra).]

Qatadah said: "It was mentioned to us that the Prophet of Allah (ﷺ) used to say: 'Among the believers is one whose light shines from Madinah to ʿAdn Abyan and Sanaʿa, and beyond that. And among the believers is one whose light shines only as far as his feet.'" [Tafsir al-Tabari (27/128).]

Sufyan al-Thawri said, from Husayn, from Mujahid, from Junadah ibn Umayyah, who said: "Indeed you are written with Allah by your names, your features, your forms, your secret conversations and your gatherings. * *

As for His words: ﴿Good news for you today: gardens beneath which rivers flow﴾, meaning: it will be said to them, "Good news for you today: gardens," that is, you have glad tidings of gardens beneath which rivers flow, ﴿abiding therein﴾, meaning remaining in them forever. ﴿That is the great triumph.﴾

* *

No one will be saved on that Day except those who believed in Allah and His Messenger, acted upon what Allah commanded and abandoned what He forbade.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father told us, ʿAbdah ibn Sulayman told us, Ibn al-Mubarak told us, Safwan ibn ʿAmr told us, Sulaym ibn ʿAmir told me, who said: "We went out on a funeral at the gate of Damascus, and with us was Abu Umamah al-Bahili. From it you will move to the stations of the Day of Resurrection. You will be in some of those stations when a command from Allah overtakes people, and faces will turn white and faces will turn black. Then you will move from it to another dwelling, and a severe darkness will overtake people. Then the light will be distributed, and the believer will be given light, while the disbeliever and the hypocrite will be left and will not be given anything. So the disbeliever and the hypocrite will not benefit from the light of the believer, just as the blind does not benefit from the light of the sighted. The hypocrites will say to those who believed: ﴿Wait for us, that we may acquire some of your light.﴾ It will be said: ﴿Return behind you and seek light﴾, and this is the trick of Allah by which He deceived the hypocrites, as He said: ﴿They deceive Allah, but He is deceiving them﴾ [al-Nisa' 142]. So they return to the place where the light was distributed, but they find nothing, and they turn back to them, and between them a wall has been erected with a gate: ﴿Within it is mercy, and facing it from the direction of the torment﴾ (the verse). Sulaym ibn ʿAmir said: The hypocrite will remain deluded until the light is distributed and Allah distinguishes between the believer and the hypocrite."

Then he said: My father told us, Yahya ibn ʿUthman told us, Ibn Hayawah told us, Artat ibn al-Mundhir told us, Yusuf ibn al-Hajjaj told us, from Abu Umamah, who said: "Darkness will be sent forth on the Day of Resurrection, and no believer or disbeliever will see his own palm, until Allah sends light to the believers according to their deeds. When the hypocrites saw the believers had set out, they followed them, so Allah cast darkness over the hypocrites, and they said then: ﴿Wait for us, that we may acquire some of your light.﴾ For indeed we were with you in the world." The believers say: ﴿Return⁠﴾ from where you came, in the darkness, "and seek light there."

Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: al-Hasan ibn ʿAlawayh al-Qattan told us, Isma'il ibn ʿIsa al-ʿAttar told us, Ishaq ibn Bishr Abu Hudhayfah told us [in the Mss. But at the Sirat, Allah gives every believer a light and every hypocrite a light. When they are level on the Sirat, Allah takes away the light of the hypocrite men and women, and the hypocrites say: ﴿Wait for us, that we may acquire some of your light.﴾ The believers say: ﴿Our Lord, complete for us our light﴾ [al-Tahrim 8]. Then no one will mention anyone else at that time." [Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (11/122). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/395): "In its chain is Ishaq ibn Bishr, who is abandoned (matruk)."]

As for His words: ﴿So a wall will be set up between them, with a gate. Within it is mercy, and facing it from the direction of the torment﴾, al-Hasan and Qatadah said: it is a wall between Paradise and the Fire.

ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: it is the one Allah mentioned in His words: ﴿And between them is a barrier﴾ [al-Aʿraf 46]. The same was narrated from Mujahid, may Allah have mercy on him, and others, and this is the correct view.

﴿Within it is mercy﴾, that is, Paradise and what is in it. ﴿And facing it from the direction of the torment﴾, that is, the Fire. This was said by Qatadah, Ibn Zayd and others.

Ibn Jarir said: It has also been said that this wall is the wall of Bayt al-Maqdis, near the Valley of Hell. Then he said: Ibn al-Barqi told us, ʿAmr ibn Abi Salamah told us, from Saʿid ibn ʿAtiyyah ibn Qays, from Abu al-ʿAwwam, the muezzin of Bayt al-Maqdis, who said: I heard ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr say: "The wall that Allah mentioned in the Qur'an, ﴿So a wall will be set up between them, with a gate. Within it is mercy, and facing it from the direction of the torment﴾, is the eastern wall. Its inner side is the mosque and what adjoins it, and its outer side is the Valley of Hell."

Then it is narrated from ʿUbadah ibn al-Samit, Kaʿb al-Ahbar and ʿAli ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-ʿAbidin similar to this. This is to be understood from them as their intention to bring the meaning closer and to give an example of it, not that this specific wall, the mosque itself, and what lies beyond it of the well-known valley of Hell, is what the Qur'an means. For Paradise is in the heavens, in the highest ʿIlliyyin, and the Fire is in the lowest depths, the bottom of the lowest. As for the statement of Kaʿb al-Ahbar that the gate mentioned in the Qur'an is the Gate of Mercy, which is one of the gates of the mosque, this is among his Israelite narrations and nonsense. What is meant is a wall set up on the Day of Resurrection to separate the believers from the hypocrites. When the believers reach it, they enter through its gate. When they have completed their entry, the gate is closed, and the hypocrites remain behind it in confusion, darkness and torment, just as they were in the worldly life, in disbelief, ignorance, doubt and bewilderment. ﴿They will call out to them, "Were we not with you?"﴾, meaning: the hypocrites will call out to the believers, "Were we not with you in the worldly abode, witnessing the Friday prayers with you, praying the congregational prayers with you, standing with you at ʿArafat, attending the military campaigns with you, and performing all the obligatory acts with you?" ﴿They will say, "Yes"⁠﴾, meaning: the believers answered the hypocrites, saying, "Yes, you were with us. ﴿But you afflicted yourselves, and you waited, and you doubted, and false hopes deluded you⁠﴾." Some of the early scholars said: meaning, you afflicted yourselves with pleasures, sins and desires. ﴿And you waited⁠﴾, meaning you delayed repentance from time to time. Qatadah said: ﴿And you waited⁠﴾ for the truth and its people, ﴿and you doubted⁠﴾, meaning about the resurrection after death. ﴿And false hopes deluded you⁠﴾, meaning you said: "We will be forgiven." It was also said: the worldly life deluded you. ﴿Until the command of Allah came⁠﴾, meaning you remained in this until death came. ﴿And the Deceiver deluded you concerning Allah⁠﴾, meaning Satan.

Qatadah said: They were under a deception from Satan, and by Allah they remained upon it until Allah cast them into the Fire.

The meaning of this statement from the believers to the hypocrites is: You were with us in bodies that had no intention and no hearts with them, and you were in doubt and uncertainty, showing off to people and mentioning Allah only a little.

Mujahid said: The hypocrites were with the believers while alive, marrying them, deceiving them and associating with them, but they were with them as dead. On the Day of Resurrection they will all be given light, but the light of the hypocrites will be extinguished when they reach the wall, and at that time they will be separated.

That was said by them in the manner of rebuke and reproach to themselves. Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿So the intercession of the intercessors will not benefit them﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 48], just as He said here: ﴿So today no ransom will be taken from you, nor from those who disbelieved﴾. That is, even if one of you came today with the earth filled with gold, and the like of it along with it, in order to ransom himself from the punishment of Allah, it would not be accepted from him.
