Then he said: My father told us, Yahya ibn ʿUthman told us, Ibn Hayawah told us, Artat ibn al-Mundhir told us, Yusuf ibn al-Hajjaj told us, from Abu Umamah, who said: "Darkness will be sent forth on the Day of Resurrection, and no believer or disbeliever will see his own palm, until Allah sends light to the believers according to their deeds. The hypocrites will follow them and say: ﴿Wait for us, that we may acquire some of your light.﴾"

Al-ʿAwfi, al-Dahhak and others said, from Ibn ʿAbbas: "While people are in darkness, Allah sends forth light. When the believers see the light, they head toward it, and the light was a guide from Allah to Paradise. When the hypocrites saw the believers had set out, they followed them, so Allah cast darkness over the hypocrites, and they said then: ﴿Wait for us, that we may acquire some of your light.﴾ For indeed we were with you in the world." The believers say: ﴿Return⁠﴾ from where you came, in the darkness, "and seek light there."

Abu al-Qasim al-Tabarani said: al-Hasan ibn ʿAlawayh al-Qattan told us, Isma'il ibn ʿIsa al-ʿAttar told us, Ishaq ibn Bishr Abu Hudhayfah told us [in the Mss. "Ibn", but the correct reading is what we have adopted from al-Mu'jam al-Kabir], Ibn Jurayj told us, from Ibn Abi Mulaykah, from Ibn ʿAbbas, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Allah will call people on the Day of Resurrection by their names, as a veil from Him over His servants. But at the Sirat, Allah gives every believer a light and every hypocrite a light. When they are level on the Sirat, Allah takes away the light of the hypocrite men and women, and the hypocrites say: ﴿Wait for us, that we may acquire some of your light.﴾ The believers say: ﴿Our Lord, complete for us our light﴾ [al-Tahrim 8]. Then no one will mention anyone else at that time." [Al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (11/122). Al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (10/395): "In its chain is Ishaq ibn Bishr, who is abandoned (matruk)."]

As for His words: ﴿So a wall will be set up between them, with a gate. Within it is mercy, and facing it from the direction of the torment﴾, al-Hasan and Qatadah said: it is a wall between Paradise and the Fire.

ʿAbd al-Rahman ibn Zayd ibn Aslam said: it is the one Allah mentioned in His words: ﴿And between them is a barrier﴾ [al-Aʿraf 46]. The same was narrated from Mujahid, may Allah have mercy on him, and others, and this is the correct view.

﴿Within it is mercy﴾, that is, Paradise and what is in it. ﴿And facing it from the direction of the torment﴾, that is, the Fire. This was said by Qatadah, Ibn Zayd and others.

Ibn Jarir said: It has also been said that this wall is the wall of Bayt al-Maqdis, near the Valley of Hell. Then he said: Ibn al-Barqi told us, ʿAmr ibn Abi Salamah told us, from Saʿid ibn ʿAtiyyah ibn Qays, from Abu al-ʿAwwam, the muezzin of Bayt al-Maqdis, who said: I heard ʿAbdullah ibn ʿAmr say: "The wall that Allah mentioned in the Qur'an, ﴿So a wall will be set up between them, with a gate. Within it is mercy, and facing it from the direction of the torment﴾, is the eastern wall. Its inner side is the mosque and what adjoins it, and its outer side is the Valley of Hell."

Then it is narrated from ʿUbadah ibn al-Samit, Kaʿb al-Ahbar and ʿAli ibn al-Husayn Zayn al-ʿAbidin similar to this. This is to be understood from them as their intention to bring the meaning closer and to give an example of it, not that this specific wall, the mosque itself, and what lies beyond it of the well-known valley of Hell, is what the Qur'an means. For Paradise is in the heavens, in the highest ʿIlliyyin, and the Fire is in the lowest depths, the bottom of the lowest. As for the statement of Kaʿb al-Ahbar that the gate mentioned in the Qur'an is the Gate of Mercy, which is one of the gates of the mosque, this is among his Israelite narrations and nonsense. What is meant is a wall set up on the Day of Resurrection to separate the believers from the hypocrites. When the believers reach it, they enter through its gate. When they have completed their entry, the gate is closed, and the hypocrites remain behind it in confusion, darkness and torment, just as they were in the worldly life, in disbelief, ignorance, doubt and bewilderment. ﴿They will call out to them, "Were we not with you?"﴾, meaning: the hypocrites will call out to the believers, "Were we not with you in the worldly abode, witnessing the Friday prayers with you, praying the congregational prayers with you, standing with you at ʿArafat, attending the military campaigns with you, and performing all the obligatory acts with you?" ﴿They will say, "Yes"⁠﴾, meaning: the believers answered the hypocrites, saying, "Yes, you were with us. ﴿But you afflicted yourselves, and you waited, and you doubted, and false hopes deluded you⁠﴾." Some of the early scholars said: meaning, you afflicted yourselves with pleasures, sins and desires. ﴿And you waited⁠﴾, meaning you delayed repentance from time to time. Qatadah said: ﴿And you waited⁠﴾ for the truth and its people, ﴿and you doubted⁠﴾, meaning about the resurrection after death. ﴿And false hopes deluded you⁠﴾, meaning you said: "We will be forgiven." It was also said: the worldly life deluded you. ﴿Until the command of Allah came⁠﴾, meaning you remained in this until death came. ﴿And the Deceiver deluded you concerning Allah⁠﴾, meaning Satan.

Qatadah said: They were under a deception from Satan, and by Allah they remained upon it until Allah cast them into the Fire.

The meaning of this statement from the believers to the hypocrites is: You were with us in bodies that had no intention and no hearts with them, and you were in doubt and uncertainty, showing off to people and mentioning Allah only a little.

Mujahid said: The hypocrites were with the believers while alive, marrying them, deceiving them and associating with them, but they were with them as dead. On the Day of Resurrection they will all be given light, but the light of the hypocrites will be extinguished when they reach the wall, and at that time they will be separated.

This statement from the believers does not contradict their other statement which Allah reported about them, where He says—and He is the most truthful of speakers—: ﴿Every soul is held in pledge for what it has earned, except the companions of the right, who will be in gardens, questioning one another about the criminals: "What has led you into Saqar?" They will say: "We were not of those who prayed, nor did we feed the poor, and we used to plunge into vain discourse with the plungers, and we used to deny the Day of Recompense until certainty came to us."﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 38-47]. That was said by them in the manner of rebuke and reproach to themselves. Then He, exalted is He, said: ﴿So the intercession of the intercessors will not benefit them﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 48], just as He said here: ﴿So today no ransom will be taken from you, nor from those who disbelieved﴾. That is, even if one of you came today with the earth filled with gold, and the like of it along with it, in order to ransom himself from the punishment of Allah, it would not be accepted from him.
* *
His saying: ﴿Your abode is the Fire﴾ means: it is your destination, and to it is your return.
* *
His saying: ﴿It is your protector﴾ means: it is more fitting for you than any other abode, because of your disbelief and your doubt. And wretched is the destination.

Allah the Exalted says: Has the time not come for the believers that their hearts should humble themselves to the remembrance of Allah? That is, they should become soft at the remembrance, the admonition, and the hearing of the Qur'an, so that they understand it, submit to it, listen to it, and obey it.

Abdullah ibn al-Mubarak said: Salih al-Murri narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Ibn Abbas, that he said: Allah found the hearts of the Muhajirun (the emigrants) slow to respond, so He admonished them at the end of thirteen years of the revelation of the Qur'an, saying: ﴿Has the time not come for those who believe that their hearts should humble themselves to the remembrance of Allah?﴾, to the end of the verse. Ibn Abi Hatim narrated it, from al-Hasan ibn Muhammad ibn al-Sabbah, from Husayn al-Marwazi, from Ibn al-Mubarak, with it.

Then he and Muslim said: Yunus ibn Abd al-A'la narrated to us, Ibn Wahb informed us, Amr ibn al-Harith informed me, from Sa'id ibn Abi Hilal, meaning al-Layth, from Awn ibn Abd Allah, from his father, from Ibn Mas'ud, may Allah be pleased with him, who said: "There was no time between our accepting Islam and Allah admonishing us with this verse, ﴿Has the time not come for those who believe that their hearts should humble themselves to the remembrance of Allah?﴾ [the verse], except four years." [Sahih Muslim, no. 3027.]

This is how Muslim narrated it at the end of his book. An-Nasa'i narrated it at the commentary of this verse, from Harun ibn Sa'id al-Aili, from Ibn Wahb, with it. [Sunan an-Nasa'i al-Kubra, no. 11568.] Ibn Majah narrated it from the hadith of Musa ibn Ya'qub al-Zam'i, from Abu Hazm, from Amir ibn Abd Allah ibn al-Zubayr, from his father, similarly, and so he made it part of the Musnad of Ibn al-Zubayr. [Sunan Ibn Majah, no. 4192.] However, al-Bazzar narrated it in his Musnad by way of Musa ibn Ya'qub, from Abu Hazim, from Amir, from Ibn al-Zubayr, from Ibn Mas'ud, and mentioned it. [Musnad al-Bazzar, no. 1443, and he said: "We do not know that Ibn al-Zubayr narrated from Ibn Mas'ud except this hadith."]

Sufyan ath-Thawri said, from al-Mas'udi, from al-Qasim, who said: The Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) became bored with a boredom, so they said: "Relate to us, O Messenger of Allah." So Allah the Exalted revealed: ﴿We relate to you the best of stories﴾ [Yusuf: 3]. He said: Then they became bored again and said: "Relate to us, O Messenger of Allah," so Allah revealed: ﴿Allah has sent down the best statement﴾ [az-Zumar: 23]. Then they became bored again and said: "Relate to us, O Messenger of Allah." So Allah revealed: ﴿Has the time not come for those who believe that their hearts should humble themselves to the remembrance of Allah?﴾ [Ibn Jarir narrated it in his Tafsir (the exegesis), 15/552, Ma'arif edition, by way of al-Mas'udi from Awn ibn Abd Allah, similarly, as a mursal report (one missing a companion from its chain), without the witness mentioned here.]

Qatadah said: ﴿Has the time not come for those who believe that their hearts should humble themselves to the remembrance of Allah?﴾ It was mentioned to us that Shaddad ibn Aws used to narrate from the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) that he said: "The first thing that will be lifted from the people is humility (khushu')." [At-Tabari narrated it in his Tafsir, 27/131, and at-Tabarani connected it in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir, 7/295, narrating it by way of Imran al-Qattan, from Qatadah, from al-Hasan, from Shaddad ibn Aws, as a marfu' (traced to the Prophet) report. Imran al-Qattan is subject to criticism.]

* *

His saying: ﴿And do not be like those who were given the Book before, and the time grew long for them, so their hearts hardened﴾. Allah forbade the believers from imitating those who carried the Book before them, from the Jews and Christians. When the time grew long for them, they altered the Book of Allah that was in their hands, bought with it a small price, cast it behind their backs, turned to divergent opinions and perverted sayings, imitated men in the religion of Allah, and took their rabbis and monks as lords besides Allah. At that point their hearts hardened, so they accept no admonition, and their hearts are not softened by promise or threat.

﴿And many of them are defiant transgressors﴾, that is, in their deeds. Their hearts are corrupt and their deeds are void. As He said: ﴿So for their breaking of their covenant, We cursed them and made their hearts hard. They distort words from their places and have forgotten a portion of what they were reminded of﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 13]. That is, their hearts became corrupt, so they hardened, and distorting words from their places became part of their nature. They abandoned the deeds they were commanded to do and committed what they were forbidden. Therefore Allah forbade the believers to imitate them in any matter, whether of fundamental or subsidiary affairs.

Ibn Abi Hatim said: My father narrated to us, Hisham ibn Ammar narrated to us, Shihab ibn Khirash narrated to us, Hajjaj ibn Dinar narrated to us, from Mansur ibn al-Mu'tamir, from al-Rabi' ibn Abi Amilah al-Fazari, who said: Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud narrated to us a hadith, and I have never heard anything more wonderful to me than it, except something from the Book of Allah, or something the Prophet (ﷺ) said. He said: "Indeed, the Children of Israel, when the time grew long for them and their hearts hardened, invented a book from their own selves. Their hearts were enamored of it, their tongues found it lawful, and they took delight in it. The truth stood between them and many of their desires, so they said: 'Come, let us call the Children of Israel to this book of ours. Whoever follows us in it, we will leave him alone, and whoever dislikes following us, we will kill him.' They did so. Among them was a jurist (faqih) who, when he saw what they were doing, went to what he knew of the Book of Allah, wrote it on a small piece, folded it, placed it in a horn, and hung that horn around his neck. When they multiplied the killing, some of them said to others: 'O people, you have spread killing among the Children of Israel. Call so-and-so and present your book to him. If he follows you, the rest of the people will follow you, and if he refuses, kill him.' They called that jurist, so-and-so, and said: 'Do you believe in what is in our book?' He said: 'And what is in it? Present it to me.' They presented it to him to the end. Then they said: 'Do you believe in this?' He said: 'Yes, I believed in what is in this,' and he pointed with his hand to the horn. So they left him. When he died, they dug him up and found the horn hanging on him, and they found in it what he knew of the Book of Allah. Some of them said to others: 'O people, we did not used to hear this. He was afflicted by a trial.' Thus the Children of Israel split into seventy-two sects, and the best of their sects was the sect of the People of the Two Horns (Dhu al-Qarnayn's companions)."

Ibn Mas'ud said: "Indeed, it is near for you, if you remain (or whoever remains of you), that you will see matters you deny, for which you cannot find any change. So it is enough for a person among you that Allah knows from his heart that he hates them."

Abu Ja'far at-Tabari said: Ibn Humayd narrated to us, Jarir narrated to us, from Mughirah, from Abu Ma'shar, from Ibrahim, who said: Utarais ibn Urquib came to Ibn Mas'ud and said: "O Abu Abd Allah, ruined is the one who does not enjoin good and forbid evil." Abd Allah said: "Ruined is the one whose heart does not know what is good and whose heart does not reject what is evil. Indeed, when the time grew long for the Children of Israel and their hearts hardened, they invented a book from between their hands and their feet. Their hearts were enamored of it, their tongues found it lawful, and they said: 'We will present this book to the Children of Israel. Whoever believes in it, we will leave him alone, and whoever disbelieves in it, we will kill him.'" He said: "One of them put the Book of Allah in a horn, then placed the horn between his breasts. When he was asked, 'Do you believe in this?' he said, 'I believe in it,' pointing to the horn between his breasts, 'and why would I not believe in this Book?' So among the best of their sects today is the sect of the Companion of the Horn." [Tafsir at-Tabari, 27/132.]

As for His saying: ﴿And those who believe in Allah and His messengers - those are the siddiqun (the truthful, sincere ones)﴾, this completes the sentence describing those who believe in Allah and His messengers as siddiqun.

Al-'Awfi related from Ibn 'Abbas concerning His saying: ﴿And those who believe in Allah and His messengers - those are the siddiqun﴾, that this is a separate statement, followed by ﴿And the martyrs with their Lord, they will have their reward and their light﴾.

Abu al-Duha said: ﴿Those are the siddiqun﴾, then he began a new statement, saying: ﴿And the martyrs with their Lord﴾. Likewise said Masruq, al-Dahhak, Muqatil ibn Hayyan, and others.

Al-A'mash related from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, from 'Abd Allah (Ibn Mas'ud) concerning His saying: ﴿Those are the siddiqun and the martyrs with their Lord﴾, that he said: "They are three categories: meaning the believers (al-Musaddiqin), the siddiqin, and the martyrs," just as Allah, exalted is He, said: ﴿And whoever obeys Allah and the Messenger - those are with the ones upon whom Allah has bestowed favour, of the prophets, the siddiqin, the martyrs and the righteous﴾ [An-Nisa: 69]. * *

Ibn Kathir (may Allah have mercy on him) said:

He, may He be exalted, informs about His decree that preceded His creation, before He brought the creatures into being. He says: ﴿No calamity befalls in the earth or in yourselves⦆ — that is, in the horizons and in your souls — ﴿but it is in a Book before We bring it into being⦆ — that is, before We create the creation and bring the soul into existence.

Some of them said: the pronoun in ﴿before We bring it into being﴾ refers to the souls (anfus). It was also said that it refers to the calamity. The best view is that it refers to the creation and the creatures (al-khaliqah wal-bariyyah), because the context points to them, as Ibn Jarir said:

Ya'qub related to me: Ibn 'Ulayyah related to us, from Mansur ibn 'Abd al-Rahman, who said: I was sitting with al-Hasan when a man said: "Ask him about His saying: ﴿No calamity befalls in the earth or in yourselves but it is in a Book before We bring it into being⦆." So I asked him about it, and he said: "Glory be to Allah! And who would doubt this? Every calamity between heaven and earth is in the Book of Allah before He brings the soul into being." [[Tafsir al-Tabari (27/135).]]

As for His words: ﴿And We sent down iron, wherein is great might﴾, meaning We made iron a deterrent for those who refuse the truth and oppose it after the proof has been established against them. All of them were argument against the polytheists, and explanation and clarification of Tawhid, and proofs. When the proof had been established against those who opposed (in another narration: "against those among them who lagged behind"), Allah prescribed the hijrah and commanded them to fight with swords, striking necks and skulls, against those who opposed the Qur'an, denied it, and defied it.

Imam Ahmad and Abu Dawud related, from the hadith of Abd al-Rahman ibn Thabit ibn Thawban, from Hassan ibn Atiyyah, from Abu al-Munib al-Jurashi al-Shami, from Ibn Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "I was sent with the sword before the Hour, until Allah is worshipped alone with no partner. My provision has been placed under the shade of my spear, and humiliation and disgrace have been placed upon those who oppose my command. Whoever imitates a people is one of them." * *

As for His words: ﴿And that Allah may know who supports Him and His messengers unseen﴾, meaning whoever's intention in carrying weapons is to support Allah and His messengers. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Powerful and Exalted in Might﴾, meaning He is Powerful and Exalted in Might; He supports whoever supports Him without needing people. * *

* *

The other is: We did not prescribe that for them; We prescribed for them only the seeking of God's pleasure.

* *

Ibn Abi Hatim said: Ishaq ibn Abi Hamzah Abu Ya'qub al-Razi related to us, al-Sindi ibn Abd Rabbih [[In M: "al-Sindi ibn Abd Rabbih"; in A: "al-Sarri ibn Abd Rabbih".]] related to us, Bukayr ibn Ma'ruf related to us, from Muqatil ibn Hayyan, from al-Qasim ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abd Allah ibn Mas'ud, from his father, from his grandfather, Ibn Mas'ud, who said: The Messenger of God ﷺ said to me: "O Ibn Mas'ud." I said: "At your service, O Messenger of God." He said: "Do you know that the Children of Israel split into seventy-two sects? Only three of them were saved. They rose up among the kings and tyrants after Jesus, son of Mary, peace be upon him. They called to the religion of God and the religion of Jesus, son of Mary, so they fought the tyrants, and they were killed; they were patient and were saved. Then another group arose which had no strength for fighting, so they stood among the kings and tyrants and called to the religion of God and the religion of Jesus, son of Mary, and they were killed, cut with saws, and burned with fire; they were patient and were saved. Then another group arose which had no strength for fighting and could not uphold justice, so they retreated to the mountains, worshipped, and lived as monks. They are the ones whom God, Mighty and Majestic, mentioned: ﴿But monasticism, they invented it; We did not prescribe it for them﴾." [[Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (10/211) through Hisham ibn Ammar, from al-Walid ibn Muslim, from Bukayr ibn Ma'ruf, similarly; Bukayr ibn Ma'ruf is subject to criticism.]]

[[Tafsir al-Tabari (27/138).]]

The reliability of this chain is not undermined by the condition of Dawud ibn al-Muhabbar, for he is one of the fabricators of hadith; but it has been transmitted by Abu Ya'la with its chain from Shayban ibn Farrukh, from al-Sa'iq ibn Hazn, with the same content. [[Narrated by al-Tabarani in al-Mu'jam al-Kabir (10/272) through Muhammad al-Hadrami, from Shayban, similarly; narrated by al-Hakim in al-Mustadrak (2/480) through Abd al-Rahman ibn al-Mubarak, from al-Sa'iq ibn Hazn, similarly. Among them were believers who read the Torah and the Gospel. It was said to their kings: "We find nothing more severe than the insults these people hurl at us. So call them, and let them recite as we recite, and let them believe as we believe." He summoned them, gathered them, and offered them death or to abandon the recitation of the Torah and the Gospel, except for what they had altered from them. They said: "What do you want from us? Leave us alone." A group of them said: "Build for us a pillar, then raise us upon it, and give us something with which to lift our food and drink, so that we will not come down to you." Another group said: "Let us wander the earth and roam, and drink as the wild beasts drink; if you can seize us in your land, then kill us." Another group said: "Build for us houses in the wilderness, and we will dig wells and cultivate herbs, so that we will not come back to you and will not pass by you." There was no tribe that did not have a close relative among them. They did that, and God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿But monasticism, they invented it; We did not prescribe it for them, except seeking the pleasure of God, but they did not observe it with its proper observance﴾. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (27/138) and Sunan al-Nasa'i (8/231).]]

This narration contains strangeness, and the explanation of these two verses will come later in a different manner, and God knows best.

He said: "How well I know them and their people! These are the people of these dwellings. Rebellion and envy destroyed them. [[Al-Musnad (3/266); in it is Zayd al-'Ammi, who is weak.]]

Ibn Jarir and Abu Abd al-Rahman al-Nasa'i — and the wording is his — said: al-Husayn ibn Hurayth informed us, al-Fadl ibn Musa related to us, from Sufyan ibn Sa'id, from Ata' ibn al-Sa'ib, from Sa'id ibn Jubayr, from Ibn Abbas, may God be pleased with both of them, who said: There were kings after Jesus, peace be upon him, who altered the Torah and the Gospel. Among them were believers who read the Torah and the Gospel. It was said to their kings: "We find nothing more severe than the insults these people hurl at us. They recite: ﴿And whoever does not judge by what God has revealed, they are the disbelievers﴾ [al-Ma'idah: 44], these verses, along with what they reproach us for in our deeds in their recitation. So call them, and let them recite as we recite, and let them believe as we believe." He summoned them, gathered them, and offered them death or to abandon the recitation of the Torah and the Gospel, except for what they had altered from them. They said: "What do you want from us? Leave us alone." A group of them said: "Build for us a pillar, then raise us upon it, and give us something with which to lift our food and drink, so that we will not come down to you." Another group said: "Let us wander the earth and roam, and drink as the wild beasts drink; if you can seize us in your land, then kill us." Another group said: "Build for us houses in the wilderness, and we will dig wells and cultivate herbs, so that we will not come back to you and will not pass by you." There was no tribe that did not have a close relative among them. They did that, and God, Mighty and Majestic, revealed: ﴿But monasticism, they invented it; We did not prescribe it for them, except seeking the pleasure of God, but they did not observe it with its proper observance﴾. As for the others, they said: "We will worship as so-and-so worshipped, and wander as so-and-so wandered, and take houses as so-and-so took," while they were upon their polytheism, having no knowledge of the faith of those whom they followed [[In M: "به".]]. When the Prophet ﷺ was sent, few of them remained: a man came down from his hermitage, a wanderer came from his wandering, and the monk came from his monastery, and they believed in him and affirmed him. God, Mighty and Majestic, then said: ﴿O you who believe, fear God and believe in His Messenger; He will give you a double portion of His mercy﴾, two rewards for their faith in Jesus, son of Mary, the Torah and the Gospel, and for their faith in Muhammad ﷺ and their affirmation [of him]. He said, as in ﴿And He will make for you a light by which you walk﴾ [al-Hadid: 28]: this is the Qur'an, and their following the Prophet ﷺ. He said: ﴿So that the People of the Book may know﴾ — those who imitate you — ﴿that they have no power over anything of God's bounty, and that bounty is in God's hand; He gives it to whom He wills, and God is the Possessor of great bounty﴾. [[Tafsir al-Tabari (27/138) and Sunan al-Nasa'i (8/231).]]

This narration contains strangeness, and the explanation of these two verses will come later in a different manner, and God knows best.

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la al-Mawsili said: Ahmad ibn Isa related to us, Abd Allah ibn Wahb related to us, Sa'id ibn Abd al-Rahman ibn Abi al-Ama' related to me: that Sahl ibn Abi Umamah narrated to him that he and his father entered upon Anas ibn Malik in Medina during the time of Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz, while he was governor. He was praying a light prayer, as if it were the prayer of a traveller or close to it. When he finished the greeting, [Sahl's father] said: "May God have mercy on you, was this the obligatory prayer, or something voluntary you performed?" He said: "It is the obligatory prayer, and it is the prayer of the Messenger of God ﷺ. I have not erred except in something I forgot. The Messenger of God, may God's blessings and peace be upon him, used to say: 'Do not make things hard on yourselves, lest they be made hard upon you, for a people made things hard on themselves and so it was made hard upon them; those are their remnants in the monasteries and the hermitages: ﴿monasticism, they invented it; We did not prescribe it for them﴾.'" Then they went out the next morning and said: "Let us ride and look and take heed." He said: "Yes." So they all rode, and suddenly they came upon deserted dwellings whose people had perished, become extinct and vanished, fallen upon their roofs. They said: "Do you know these dwellings?" He said: "How well I know them and their people! These are the people of these dwellings. Rebellion and envy destroyed them. Envy extinguishes the light of good deeds; rebellion either confirms that or denies it. The eye commits fornication, and the hand, the foot, the body and the tongue; and the private parts either confirm that or deny it." [[Musnad Abi Ya'la (6/365).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Ya'mur related to us, Abd Allah related to us, Sufyan informed us, from Zayd al-'Ammi, from Abu Iyas, from Anas ibn Malik, that the Prophet ﷺ said: "Every prophet has a monasticism, and the monasticism of this nation is jihad in the way of God, Mighty and Majestic." [[Al-Musnad (3/266); in it is Zayd al-'Ammi, who is weak.]]

Al-Hafiz Abu Ya'la narrated it from Abd Allah ibn Muhammad ibn Asma', from Abd Allah ibn al-Mubarak, with the wording: "Every nation has a monasticism, and the monasticism of this nation is jihad in the way of God." [[Musnad Abi Ya'la (7/210).]]

Imam Ahmad said: Husayn — that is, Ibn Muhammad — related to us, Ibn Ayyash — meaning Isma'il — related to us, from al-Hajjaj ibn Marwan [[In M: "Harun".]] al-Kala'i, and Uqayl ibn Mudrik al-Sulami, from Abu Sa'id al-Khudri, may God be pleased with him, that a man came to him and said: "Advise me." He said: "You have asked what you asked the Messenger of God ﷺ before you. I advise you to fear God, for it is the head of everything. Upon you is jihad, for it is the monasticism of Islam. Upon you is the remembrance of God and recitation of the Qur'an, for it is your spirit in heaven and your remembrance on earth." Ahmad alone narrated it. [[Al-Musnad (3/82); al-Haythami said in al-Majma' (4/215): "The men of Ahmad are trustworthy."]]

Ibn Kathir's commentary on surah 57, verses 28–29:

It has already been mentioned, in the narration of al-Nasa'i from Ibn 'Abbas, that he understood this verse as referring to the believers among the People of the Book, and that they are given their reward twice, as in the verse in surah al-Qasas [[See the commentary on verse 54.]], and as in the hadith of al-Sha'bi from Abu Burda, from Abu Musa al-Ash'ari, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Three people will be given their reward twice: a man from the People of the Book who believed in his prophet and believed in me, he has two rewards; a slave who fulfilled the right of Allah and the right of his masters, he has two rewards; and a man who disciplined his slave-girl well, then freed her and married her, he has two rewards." [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 97, and Sahih Muslim, no. 154.]] Both of them (al-Bukhari and Muslim) recorded it in their Sahihs.

Al-Dahhak, 'Utba ibn Abi Hakim, and others agreed with Ibn 'Abbas on this interpretation, and it is the view preferred by Ibn Jarir.

Sa'id ibn Jubayr said: When the People of the Book boasted that they would be given their reward twice, Allah revealed this verse concerning this Ummah: ﴿O you who believe, fear Allah and believe in His Messenger; He will give you a double portion (kiflayn) of His mercy﴾, meaning, two multiples. And He added: ﴿and He will make for you a light by which you will walk﴾, meaning, guidance by which one sees clearly, away from blindness and ignorance, ﴿and forgive you﴾. Thus He favoured them with the light and forgiveness. Ibn Jarir narrated it from him.

This verse is like His saying, exalted is He: ﴿O you who believe, if you fear Allah, He will grant you a criterion (furqan) and will remove from you your misdeeds and forgive you. And Allah is the possessor of great bounty﴾ [al-Anfal: 29].

Sa'id ibn 'Abd al-'Aziz said: 'Umar ibn al-Khattab asked a rabbi of the Jewish scholars: "What is the greatest multiplication that is given for one good deed to you?" He said: "A kifl (portion) of three hundred and fifty good deeds." 'Umar then praised Allah because He had given us two kifls. Then Sa'id mentioned the saying of Allah, exalted and mighty is He: ﴿He will give you two kifls of His mercy﴾. Sa'id said: "The two kifls in (the reward for) Friday are like that." Ibn Jarir narrated it.

Among what supports this view is what Imam Ahmad narrated: Isma'il narrated to us, Ayyub narrated to us, from Nafi', from Ibn 'Umar, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Your example, and the example of the Jews and the Christians, is like a man who employed workers and said: 'Who will work for me from the morning prayer until midday for a qirat each?' So the Jews worked. Then he said: 'Who will work for me from midday until the afternoon prayer for a qirat each?' So the Christians worked. Then he said: 'Who will work for me from the afternoon prayer until sunset for two qirats each?' Indeed, you are the ones who worked. The Christians and the Jews became angry and said: 'We did more work and received less pay.' He said: 'Have I wronged you in any of your wages?' They said: 'No.' He said: 'Then it is only My bounty, which I give to whom I will.'" [[Al-Musnad, 2/6.]]

Ahmad said: Mu'ammal also narrated it to us, from Sufyan, from 'Abd Allah ibn Dinar, from Ibn 'Umar, similar to the hadith of Nafi', from him. [[Al-Musnad, 2/111.]]

Al-Bukhari alone recorded it. He narrated it from Sulayman ibn Harb, from Hammad, from Ayyub, from Nafi', with the same wording, [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 2268.]] and from Qutayba, from al-Layth, from Nafi', with similar wording. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 3459.]]

Al-Bukhari also said: Muhammad ibn al-'Ala' narrated to me, Abu Usama narrated to us, from Buraid, from Abu Burda, from Abu Musa, from the Prophet (ﷺ), who said: "The example of the Muslims, the Jews, and the Christians is like a man who hired people to do a task for him for a day until night, for a known wage. They worked until midday and said: 'We have no need of your wage which you stipulated for us, and what we have done is worthless.' He said to them: 'Do not do that. Complete the rest of your work and take your full wage.' But they refused and left. He hired others after them and said: 'Complete the rest of your day, and you will have the wage I stipulated for them.' They worked until the time of the afternoon prayer, then they said: 'What we have done is worthless, and yours is the wage you set for us.' He said: 'Complete the rest of your work, for what remains of the day is a small amount.' But they refused. So he hired another group to work for him for the rest of their day, and they worked the rest of their day until the sun set. They received the full wage of both groups. That is their example, and the example of what they accepted of this light." Al-Bukhari alone recorded it. [[Sahih al-Bukhari, no. 2271.]]

For this reason He, exalted is He, said: ﴿So that the People of the Book may know that they have no power over anything of the bounty of Allah﴾, meaning, so that they may be certain that they cannot reject what Allah has given, nor give what Allah has withheld, ﴿and that bounty is in the hand of Allah; He gives it to whom He wills, and Allah is the possessor of great bounty﴾.

Ibn Jarir said: "﴿So that (li-'allā) he may know﴾" means "so that (li-ya'lam) he may know." It is reported that Ibn Mas'ud recited it as "li-kay ya'lam," and likewise Hittan ibn 'Abd Allah and Sa'id ibn Jubayr. Ibn Jarir said: This is because the Arabs make "la" (lā) a redundant particle (ṣila) in any speech where a negation that is not explicit enters at its beginning and end. The example at the beginning is His saying: ﴿What prevented you from prostrating?﴾ [al-A'raf: 12]; ﴿And what will make you aware that when it comes they will not believe?﴾ [al-An'am: 109]; ﴿And it is forbidden for a town which We destroyed that they will not return﴾ [al-Anbiya': 95].
